title: Classic Pecan Pie
summary: A partly baked shell filled with a brown-sugar and golden-syrup custard full of toasted pecans, baked low and slow so it sets evenly without bubbling over.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
cold unsalted butter, cut into 1 cm cubes
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Combine the 180 g flour with the sugar and salt, then cut in the 120 g cold butter until pea-size bits remain. Work in the 60 ml ice-cold water, plus up to 15 ml more if the dough will not hold when pinched. Flatten, wrap and chill 1 h.

steps.title: Roll and crimp
steps.text: Roll the dough to a 30 cm round roughly 3 mm thick, lift it into the 23 cm pie dish and trim to a 1 cm overhang. Fold the edge under, crimp it high, and chill 30 min; a tall rim holds the generous filling.

steps.title: Part-bake the shell
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan). Prick the base, line with baking paper and beans and bake 20 min, then remove them and bake 5 min more until just dry and pale golden. Part-baking keeps the base from turning gummy under the syrupy filling.

steps.title: Warm the syrup
steps.text: Lower the oven to 150 °C (130 °C fan). Warm the brown sugar, syrup, cream, molasses, butter and salt in the saucepan over medium heat, stirring, until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves; do not let it boil. Cool 5 min so it will not scramble the yolks.

steps.title: Combine the filling
steps.text: Whisk the yolks in a bowl, then whisk in the warm syrup a little at a time, followed by the vanilla. Stir in the chopped pecans. Yolks alone give a richer, smoother set than whole eggs.

steps.title: Bake low
steps.text: Pour into the warm shell, arrange the pecan halves in neat rings over the top and bake 50-60 min. It is done when the edge is set, the centre wobbles only slightly and reads about 93 °C. A low oven keeps the sugary filling from puffing, cracking or boiling over.

steps.title: Cool fully
steps.text: Cool on the rack at least 4 h before cutting into 10, as the filling keeps setting as it cools. Keep covered at cool room temperature 1 day or chilled up to 4 days.

tips: Toast the pecans first for the deepest flavour, but let them cool before stirring them in.
Common mistake: baking until the centre is firm. Take it out with a slight wobble at about 93 °C or the filling turns dry and grainy.
Golden syrup gives a clean caramel note; molasses adds depth.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at cool room temperature 1 day or in the fridge up to 4 days. Freeze up to 2 months; thaw in the fridge and serve at room temperature.
